comment: @context-free corpus for the comment-length check. Both the Go and the TypeScript checker run every case and must report the same violation kinds AND the same kind:count multiset. `expect` lists the kinds the case must produce: doc, inline, line. These rows pin the shapes listed; they are not a proof for shapes they do not list, and which divergence classes have been probed is recorded on hdf-libs-c5pbf rather than claimed here. CRLF is asserted by a unit test instead of a row, because a checked-in CRLF fixture is at the mercy of git line-ending normalization.

cases.name: doc at cap (10 lines)
doc over cap (11 lines)
inline at cap (5 lines)
inline over cap (6 lines)
comment line at cap (90 chars)
comment line over cap (91 chars)
file header over doc cap (11 lines) — header is judged as doc
a // inside a string literal is not a comment
clean file
six lines above control flow is inline, not doc
six lines above an assignment is inline, not doc
a // inside a template literal or raw string is not a comment
a trailing comment after code is measured too
an indented comment is not charged for its indentation
a block comment adjacent to line comments is one group
six lines above an import is doc, not inline
a blank line detaches a group from the declaration below it
a group ADJACENT to the declaration below it is its doc
a // inside a SUBSTITUTION template (TS) or a raw string (Go) is not a comment
a // inside a regex literal is not a comment
a header is still a header in a file that opens with a shebang
six lines above an enum member is doc in both
a /** */ header over the doc cap, with no declaration to rescue it
a /** */ header at the cap is accepted, with no declaration to rescue it
two runs separated by a blank line are two groups, not one
a file of only comments is a header
